title: Python Forge Version 1 Curriculum Architecture
description: Scalable modular curriculum hierarchy designed for mobile-first interactive Python learning.

modules.title: Python Foundations
modules.description: Master the absolute basics of executing code, handling standard input/output, and defining basic state with variables.

missions.title: Hello World
missions.description: Every programmer starts here. Forge your very first instruction to print text to the console.
missions.objective: Print exactly "Hello, World!" to the console.
hints: Text strings in Python must be enclosed in quotation marks.

missions.title: Variables
missions.description: Variables act as containers to store data values. Let's assign a value and display it.
missions.objective: Create a variable named message, assign "Python Forge" to it, then print it.
hints: Use the = operator to assign a value to a variable.
Make sure to pass the variable name directly to the print() function without using quotation marks.

missions.title: Integers
missions.description: Learn how Python stores whole numbers using integer variables.
missions.concept: Integers are whole numbers without decimal points. You can store them inside variables just like text.
missions.objective: Create a variable named age with the value 18 and print it.
hints: Use print(age) to display the value.

missions.title: Floats
missions.description: Store decimal numbers using floating-point variables.
missions.concept: Floats are numbers that contain a decimal point. They are commonly used for measurements like height, weight, or temperature.
missions.objective: Create a variable named temperature with the value 36.5 and print it.

missions.title: Strings
missions.description: Store and display text using string variables.
missions.concept: Strings represent text in Python. Text must always be enclosed in quotation marks.
missions.objective: Create a variable named city with the value "Kashmir" and print it.
hints: Text values must be inside quotation marks.
Use print(city) to display the variable.
